title: Energy (Resilience Measures and Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill
what_it_is: Energy (Resilience Measures and Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill

sections.label: EMA Act duties
sections.summary: The EMA Act gives EMA duties on market framework, market conduct, consumer interests and efficient energy use.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The EMA Act charges EMA with the duty to create a market framework for electricity and gas, promote fair and efficient market conduct, protect the interests of consumers and the public in electricity and gas supply and promote the efficient use of energy utilities.

sections.label: Decarbonising the power sector
sections.summary: The power sector accounts for about 40% of Singapore's carbon emissions, making its decarbonisation a key pillar against climate change.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: With the power sector accounting for about 40% of Singapore’s carbon emissions, decarbonising the power sector is a key pillar of our efforts to combat climate change.

sections.label: EMA power infrastructure powers
sections.summary: This empowers EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate power infrastructure to safeguard energy security and reliability.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: First, to empower EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate power infrastructure to safeguard our energy security and reliability.

sections.label: Amending Electricity Act, EMA Act
sections.summary: The first key amendment amends section 3 of the Electricity Act and the EMA Act's Second Schedule to enable EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate critical infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The first key amendment, therefore, amends section 3 of the Electricity Act and the Second Schedule of the EMA Act, to empower and enable EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate critical infrastructure.

sections.label: Offence for damaging infrastructure
sections.summary: The second key amendment updates the Electricity Act and Gas Act to make damaging certain transmission and pipeline infrastructure in Singapore's territorial waters an offence.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The second key amendment updates the Electricity Act and the Gas Act to make it an offence to damage any infrastructure housing or intended to house any transmission electricity cables, gas transmission pipeline or submarine gas pipeline in the territorial waters of Singapore.

sections.label: EMA carbon efficiency powers
sections.summary: The third key amendment empowers EMA to enhance the carbon efficiency of parties licensed under the Electricity Act.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Moving on to the third amendment, the third key amendment empowers EMA to enhance the carbon efficiency of parties licensed under the Electricity Act.

sections.label: EMA greenhouse gas regulatory functions
sections.summary: The Bill expands EMA's regulatory functions under the Electricity Act to include implementing policies and strategies connected with reducing greenhouse gas emissions in electricity import, export, generation, transmission or supply.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: The Bill expands EMA's regulatory functions under the Electricity Act to include implementing policies and strategies connected with the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions in the import, export, generation, transmission or supply of electricity.

sections.label: EMA energy efficiency incentive schemes
sections.summary: Since 2018, EMA has rolled out incentive schemes, such as the Energy Efficiency Grant for Power Generation Companies, to encourage power generation companies to improve energy efficiency.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan See Leng)
sentences.text: Since 2018, EMA has rolled out incentive schemes, such as the Energy Efficiency Grant for Power Generation Companies, to encourage power generation companies to improve energy efficiency.

sections.label: LNG infrastructure as back-up
sections.summary: MTI and EMA established LNG infrastructure about a decade ago as a back-up to piped gas supply, with 95% of electricity generated from natural gas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Credits to MTI and EMA for also establishing the liquified natural gas (LNG) infrastructure about a decade ago to serve as a back-up source to the piped gas supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This is most critical as, today, 95% of our electricity is generated from natural gas and, by far, still the cleanest fossil fuel to date.

sections.label: EMA powers over electricity infrastructure
sections.summary: The Bill empowers EMA to directly build, acquire and manage essential electricity infrastructures, issue licences, import electricity and issue bonds to finance critical facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Among others, this Bill empowers EMA to directly build, acquire and manage these essential electricity infrastructures, if need be, to ensure the resilience and security of our power supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: It also enables EMA to issue licences, import of electricity and issue bonds to finance these critical facilities.

sections.label: EMA bonds for project financing
sections.summary: The speaker supports the new provision allowing EMA to raise capital or issue bonds to finance construction of projects where necessary, as commercial returns may be inadequate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: The commercial returns from the generators may not be adequate to service such long-term debts which also come with project risks and, therefore, higher risk premiums.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Hence, I am supportive of the new provision in this amendment that allows EMA to raise capital or issue bonds to finance the construction of these projects where necessary.

sections.label: EMA transition, costs, retailer deposits
sections.summary: The passage asks how EMA will ensure a smooth transition and the estimated infrastructure cost, and notes an amendment clarifying drawdown on electricity retailers' deposits to offset settlement payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: How would EMA ensure that this transition can be smoothly carried out with no or minimal disruptions to our energy supply?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: Also, what is the estimated infrastructure cost to realise our new energy vision?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: In this Bill, there is also an amendment to clarify the ability to draw down on electricity retailers' deposits to offset outstanding settlement payments to protect consumers' interest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: This amendment is necessary in light of the disruptions in the open electricity market that we saw.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Bukit Panjang)
sentences.text: So, I urge EMA to look into further measures to mitigate these counterparty risks; including allowing for the novation of some of these in-the-money fuel hedging positions from the retailers who may have abruptly exited the market, to allow this novation of this contract, this position that they hedged on, to come to the new retailers the consumers choose, for example, SP Services, so that consumers' interests can be safeguarded.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To date, five electricity retailers will be dimming their lights and others have stopped accepting new customers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This has impacted over 150,000 customers, who will most likely have to pay more for electricity in the coming months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: About 714,000 households which had not previously switched to a retailer in the open electricity market are paying a regulated electricity tariff, which has increased by 32% since last September.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the answer to a Parliamentary Question (PQ) I asked in January, 79% of HDB 1- and 2-room households and 63% of 3-roomers are paying the regulated tariff compared to just 40% of those living in landed properties.

sections.label: Low-carbon electricity imports by 2035
sections.summary: Singapore plans to import up to four gigawatts of low-carbon electricity by 2035, about 30% of its supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Singapore is planning to import up to four gigawatts of low-carbon electricity by 2035, which is expected to make up around 30% of Singapore's electricity supply.

sections.label: Malaysia bars renewable exports
sections.summary: On 22 October, Malaysia announced it will not allow renewable energy exports to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On 22 October, Malaysia announced that it will not allow renewable energy exports to Singapore.

sections.label: Battery prices and solar target
sections.summary: Lithium-ion battery prices are expected to fall 45% from 2018 to 2030, and EMA targets two gigawatts of solar by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the same time, the price of lithium-ion batteries is expected to fall 45% between 2018 and 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: EMA has said it is targeting a two-gigawatt peak of solar energy by 2030, Yet, even if this target is met, solar will supply only around 3% of our total energy demand.

sections.label: EMA emissions standards and Genco grants
sections.summary: Empowering EMA to set emissions standards is vital, and $23 million in grants went to three power generation companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Empowering EMA to set emissions standards for power generation companies is, therefore, vital for us to realise our international climate change commitments and to truly go green.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: It has been just over a year since the EMA awarded $23 million in grants to Senoko Energy, Tuas Power Generation and YTL PowerSeraya.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Have these three companies seen their energy efficiency projects bear fruit?

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: How much does the Government expect to invest for the second Genco Energy Efficiency Grant Call, which is currently open for submission?

sections.label: Retailer exits affect household consumers
sections.summary: The Minister said the exit of these retailers affected about a tenth of household consumers in the Open Electricity Market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: According to the Minister, the exit of these retailers has affected about a tenth of household consumers in the Open Electricity Market.

sections.label: Energy crisis and market stability
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the retailer exodus will not harm the Open Electricity Market and urges more consumer protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: If the current global energy crisis persists, market prices may soon rise above the regulated tariff.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: I hope that this exodus of retailers will not end up becoming a false dawn for the Open Electricity Market and I hope that the Government can do more to ensure market stability, while ensuring that consumers continue to enjoy attractive electricity prices and more competition in the market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: But as we pursue our path towards energy self-sufficiency, we must recognise that we will continue to be a price-taker in both the short and the medium term.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: We should, therefore, do more to protect our consumers, who have the most to lose in a volatile energy market.

sections.label: Genco longevity and employment
sections.summary: The passage states that gencos' longevity and employees' long-term employment viability are concerns, with over 1,000 workers affected by the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The first of which is the longevity of the power generation companies or gencos in Singapore and the long-term employment viability for their employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: These companies currently employ more than 1,000 workers and changes to the Energy (Resilience Measures and Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill will have an impact on them.

sections.label: EMA power plant intervention concerns
sections.summary: The passage states the Bill lets EMA finance, build, own and operate a power plant, and that gencos fear regulatory risk and are reluctant to invest.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would translate to the training and upskilling of the genco workers, ensuring that their long-term employment can create exciting opportunities for new entrants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This proposed Bill provides the ability for EMA, or an entity wholly owned and/or controlled by EMA, to finance, build, own and operate a power plant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The industry players are concerned that a direct intervention by EMA in the Singapore power market may signal a market failure to the investors that have already gone through a sustained period of losses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Gencos, particularly those which are foreign-owned, are likely to regard the regulatory risk in the Singapore market as high and will be reluctant to invest in new capacity or repowering of their ageing units.

sections.label: Solar workforce training efforts
sections.summary: The passage states NTUC and e2i work with SEAS on solar workforce supply and jobs, and UPAGE and SP Group's Fusion trained over 1,600 workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: NTUC and our Employment and Employability Institute are contributing to this national effort by working with the Sustainable Energy Association of Singapore (SEAS) to increase workforce supply and redesign jobs in the solar industry to meet future demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: With this energy transition in mind, UPAGE and SP Group management have started on a journey called Fusion, which stands for Future Skills in Everyone, back in January 2018.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Through this, more than 1,600 of the workers have attended close to more than 20,260 hours of training.

sections.label: Singaporeans reducing energy use
sections.summary: The passage states all Singaporeans can reduce energy use by adopting more energy-efficient appliances and solutions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: All Singaporeans can do our part to reduce our energy use, for example, by adopting more energy-efficient appliances and solutions.

sections.label: Natural gas and energy crunch
sections.summary: The passage states 95% of Singapore's electricity is generated by natural gas and the electricity market bears the energy crunch.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: With 95% of Singapore's electricity generated by natural gas, our electricity market is bearing the full brunt of this energy crunch.

sections.label: Genco energy-efficient project awards
sections.summary: The passage states three gencos were awarded $23 million in 2020 for energy-efficient projects, equivalent to taking about 9,200 vehicles off roads annually.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In 2020, three gencos were awarded a total of $23 million for energy-efficient projects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: These projects would translate into taking about 9,200 vehicles off the roads annually.

sections.label: OEM market retailer exits
sections.summary: Analysts attribute recent exits from the OEM to the high number of retailers in the OEM market.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Analysts have suggested that the recent exits from the OEM can be attributed to the high number of retailers in the OEM market.

sections.label: Energy sector decarbonisation measures
sections.summary: The energy sector accounts for about 40% of Singapore's carbon emissions and will enhance gas plant efficiency, accelerate solar, tap regional grids and develop low-carbon solutions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The energy sector, as the Minister has said, has a key part to play as it accounts for about 40% of Singapore's carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, by enhancing the energy efficiency of natural gas power plants; second, by accelerating solar deployment; third, by tapping on regional power grids for low-carbon electricity imports; and fourth, by developing low-carbon solutions, such as hydrogen and carbon capture utilisation and storage solutions, which will enable decarbonisation in the longer term.

sections.label: EMA critical infrastructure powers
sections.summary: One amendment enables EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate critical infrastructure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Amongst the amendments is one which enables EMA to acquire, build, own and/or operate critical infrastructure.

sections.label: EMA capital raising for infrastructure
sections.summary: The amendment enables EMA to raise capital or issue bonds for infrastructure if EMA needs to step in.

sentences.speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The amendment will also enable EMA to raise capital or issue bonds for infrastructure should EMA need to step in.

sections.label: Power sector sustainability amendments
sections.summary: The proposed amendments to this Bill will ensure the sustainability, security and reliability of our power sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to this Bill will ensure the sustainability, security and reliability of our power sector.

sections.label: Diversification through four switches
sections.summary: Energy sources are diversified by harnessing four switches: natural gas, solar, regional power grids and emerging low-carbon alternatives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: First is the diversification of energy sources by harnessing four switches, namely, natural gas, solar, regional power grids and emerging low-carbon alternatives.

sections.label: Retrofitting split units with chilled water
sections.summary: Split units in residential buildings are inefficient and could be retrofitted with a centralised chilled water system using less energy per tonne.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Such new innovation implementation is necessary as current split units used in residential buildings – that is, both public and private – operate in poor energy efficiency, primarily average more than 1.5 kilowatt per tonne, because they are air-cooled and, typically, also have half or less the lifecycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: These split units could be retrofitted with a centralised chilled water system that could operate at a significantly better energy-efficient average of less than 0.65 kilowatt per tonne that capitalises on economies of scale.

sections.label: Software savings and grid energy storage
sections.summary: Software-driven approaches have estimated energy savings of 20% to 40%, and coupling Energy Storage System to gencos could improve peak demand and grid resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Based on current industry advancements, there have been proven cases that such software-driven approaches have estimated savings between 20% and 40% of energy consumption at a building and plant level.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Lastly, adopting a similar design principle from the district cooling system where cooling capacity is stored, I would like to propose coupling Energy Storage System (ESS) to existing gencos to further improve the peak capacity demand and spinning reserve.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: If there is enough ESS capacity installed in the grid, it could minimise the supply-demand mismatch on a faster and larger scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This would increase the resilience of the grid by providing more cushion to unexpected events when energy demand surges unexpectedly.

sections.label: Amendment Bill diversifying energy sources
sections.summary: The amendment Bill addresses limiting factors of the current energy strategy by diversifying energy sources and investing in new innovations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We need our economy to grow to provide good jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This amendment Bill addresses both the downside and limiting factors of our current energy strategy by boldly diversifying our energy sources, investing in new innovations to both optimise our energy usage and tapping on new forms of sustainable energy.

sections.label: Natural gas and electricity imports
sections.summary: Natural gas power plants provide over 95% of Singapore's electricity demand, and Singapore intends to import 30% of supply from low-carbon sources by 2035.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Natural gas power plants provide more than 95% of Singapore's electricity demand today.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: So, I am heartened by the recent announcement that Singapore intends to import 30% of our electricity supply from low-carbon sources by 2035, for example, through subsea cables from Indonesia and Australia.

sections.label: Drawing down electricity retailers' deposits
sections.summary: The Bill clarifies drawing down on electricity retailers' deposits to offset outstanding settlement payments, protecting consumers from default costs in insolvencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In this Bill, there are clarifications on the ability to draw down on electricity retailers' deposits to offset outstanding settlement payments and this move intends to protect consumer interests to reduce the amount of default costs borne by consumers in the event of insolvencies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: It has been reported that at least five energy retailers have announced exits, while others have stopped taking on new customers and are considering changes to their business model.

sections.label: Natural gas share in electricity generation
sections.summary: According to the National Climate Change Secretariat, natural gas used in electricity generation rose from 19% to more than 95% since 2000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: According to the National Climate Change Secretariat (NCCS), since 2000, the percentage of natural gas used in electricity generation rose from 19% to more than 95%.

sections.label: Singapore spot electricity price rise
sections.summary: EMA said the sharp rise in Singapore's spot electricity prices amid a global power crunch was exacerbated by reduced Indonesian gas supply, which has not fully recovered from July disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: As we are told by the EMA statement recently, the sharp rise in Singapore's spot electricity prices amid a global power crunch was exacerbated by a reduction in gas supply from Indonesia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Natural gas supply to Singapore from Indonesia has not fully recovered from disruptions in July, according to a news report on 18 October.

sections.label: Indonesia gas exports to Singapore
sections.summary: Natuna production fell 27.5% to 370 million standard cubic feet per day, and Indonesia said it would stop gas shipments to Singapore in 2023, with exports coming from the Corridor Block.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Production in Natuna is down 27.5% from its previous peak to 370 million standard cubic feet per day.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: In fact, in February 2020, the Energy and Mineral Resources Ministry of Indonesia said it would stop gas shipments to Singapore in the next three years to cater to domestic demand. "Gas exports to Singapore will stop in 2023 and we will use the gas for the domestic market”, Downstream Oil and Gas Regulatory Agency (BPH Migas) head Fanshurullah Asa said, as quoted from the ministry’s press release.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Indonesia's gas exports to Singapore come from the Corridor Block, which has a supply of 300 million standard cubic feet per day.

sections.label: 18-year natural gas delivery deal
sections.summary: The 18-year natural gas delivery deal was expected to start from mid-2006 via a new five-kilometre pipeline linking Petronas' Peninsular Gas Utilisation Pipeline to the Singapore Gas Transmission System.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The 18-year deal for delivery of natural gas was expected to start from mid-2006 via a new five-kilometre pipeline linking Petronas’ Peninsular Gas Utilisation Pipeline to the Singapore Gas Transmission System.

sections.label: EMA critical infrastructure powers
sections.summary: The Bill empowers EMA to acquire, build, own and operate critical infrastructure, including generation capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Next, the Bill empowers EMA to acquire, build, own and operate critical infrastructure, including generation capacity.

sections.label: EMA loans and property charges
sections.summary: With this change, EMA can now raise loans and grant charges over EMA's property.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With this change, EMA can now raise loans and grant charges over EMA’s property.

sections.label: Approval of foreign funding
sections.summary: The question asks the Minister to share in what circumstances such foreign funding would be approved by the Government.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share in what circumstances would such foreign funding be approved by the Government?

sections.label: EMA consultation and standards timeline
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can share EMA's timeline for consulting the sector and releasing new standards and policies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share EMA’s timeline for consulting the sector and for releasing new standards and policies?

sections.label: Cyber attacks on energy and water
sections.summary: The passage asks how many cyber attacks energy and water infrastructure have faced in recent years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, can the Government share how many cyber attacks have our energy and water infrastructure faced in recent years?

sections.label: Four supply switches for decarbonisation
sections.summary: Minister Tan See Leng outlined four supply switches being developed to decarbonise electricity grids.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In this year’s Committee of Supply (COS) debate, Minister Tan See Leng outlined that we are developing four "supply switches": natural gas, solar energy, regional grids and low-carbon alternatives, such as hydrogen, to decarbonise our electricity grids.

sections.label: Malaysia restricts energy exports to Singapore
sections.summary: Malaysia's Energy and Natural Resources Ministry announced only non-renewable energy may be exported to Singapore, and power sales via self-developed transmission and interconnection facilities are not allowed.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Just this month, Malaysia’s Energy and Natural Resources Ministry announced that only non-renewable energy is allowed to be exported to Singapore, and power sales through self-developed transmission and interconnection facilities to Singapore will not be allowed.

sections.label: Malaysia stance impact on LTMS-PIP
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Malaysia's change in stance affects the LTMS-PIP trial project.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share whether this change in stance from Malaysia has any impact on the trial project of the Lao PDR-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project (LTMS-PIP)?

sections.label: Grids coping with electrification demand
sections.summary: The passage asks whether electricity distribution grids and substations can cope with a surge in usage and demand from mass electrification.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Similarly, as we prepare for the pivot towards mass electrification, for example, in vehicles, I would like to ask whether the electricity distribution grids and substations will be able to cope with the surge in usage and demand.

sections.label: Manufacturing portfolio and production patterns
sections.summary: Serving industrial presence and expansion requires reviewing the manufacturing portfolio and production patterns, and possibly differentiating industrial needs from household and office demands by time of day.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: But to serve their presence and expansion involves a relook at our manufacturing portfolio as well as production patterns.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: There may be a need for us to be more precise on the roadmap of matching or differentiating their industrial activities’ needs versus the household activities and the office building demands by the time of the day.

sections.label: Allocating energy resources in disruptions
sections.summary: In critical moments, allocating energy resources among stakeholders could have far-reaching implications if supplies are disrupted or carbon commitments must be met.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: In times of critical moments, how we allocate energy resources among various stakeholders could have far-reaching implications should there be any disruption to energy supplies or the need to meet our own carbon commitments.

sections.label: Alternate supply and carbon capture
sections.summary: Material change of alternate supply from natural gas seems difficult within the coming decade, raising questions on longer-term cross-border carbon capture and storage.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: While Minister Tan See Leng has outlined the four switches for energy, it seems difficult for us to embark on any material change of alternate supply from natural gas within the coming decade.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
sentences.text: Are there opportunities in the longer term to focus on how our carbon capture capabilities and storage or utilisation can be shared cross-borders or developed in locations where underground geologic formation permits?

sections.label: Security deposit and wind-up considerations
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister about considerations for the security deposit's value, options if it is insufficient, wind-up trigger indicators, and economies of scale.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can the Minister share what are the considerations when determining the value of the security deposit?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: What are the options available in the event when the security deposit is insufficient to cover its obligations?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: What are the trigger indicators to determine that a wind-up order is necessary?

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: With the empowerment to build, own and operate, can the Minister share if there will be initiatives to ensure that there are economies of scale and synergies that are collectively accretive to the overall industry?

sections.label: GSTV U-Save rebates for HDB households
sections.summary: Households in 1- to 2-room HDB flats typically get GSTV U-Save rebates averaging about three to four months of utility bills, or about 4.5 to six months this year.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Today, households living in 1- to 2-room HDB flats, typically, benefit from GSTV U-Save rebates amounting to an average of about three to four months of the utility bills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Together with the GSTV U-Save special payments, these households will receive rebates equivalent to about 4.5 to six months of the utility bills this year.

sections.label: Singapore maximum solar potential
sections.summary: A SERIS study found Singapore has a maximum solar potential of 8 gigawatt peak by 2050.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Based on a study conducted by Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore, or SERIS, Singapore has a maximum solar potential of 8 gigawatt peak (GWp) and, that is, by 2050.

sections.label: genco fuel reserve requirement
sections.summary: Power generation companies must stockpile at least 60 days of fuel reserves for natural gas supply disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Currently, power generation companies, or gencos as we call them, are required to stockpile at least 60 days of fuel reserves in the event of disruptions to our natural gas supply.

sections.label: digital twin of electricity grid
sections.summary: EMA works with SP Group to develop a digital twin of Singapore's electricity grid for more accurate, efficient transmission and distribution.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: EMA is working closely with SP Group to develop a digital twin of Singapore's physical electricity grid, which will make the transmission and distribution more accurate and efficient.

sections.label: cyber requirements for CII Owners
sections.summary: Critical Information Infrastructure Owners must meet minimum baseline cyber requirements and report incidents to EMA and CSA within two hours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Under this framework, the energy industry's Critical Information Infrastructure Owners, the CIIOs, are required to meet minimum baseline cyber requirements, such as isolating computer systems from the Internet.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Any cyber incidents must be reported to EMA and CSA within two hours, which ensure that remedial efforts can be carried out in a timely manner.

sections.label: public consultation next year
sections.summary: The first iteration of the proposed measures may be released for public consultation as early as 2022.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The first iteration of the proposed measures may be released for public consultation as early as next year, that is 2022.

sections.label: Energy Efficiency Grant for gencos
sections.summary: S$37 million was awarded to four gencos under EMA's First Energy Efficiency Grant to adopt energy-efficient technologies and equipment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: Under EMA's First Energy Efficiency Grant for Power Generation Companies, S$37 million was awarded to four gencos to adopt energy-efficient technologies and equipment to reduce their carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: When completed, these projects are expected to reduce carbon emissions by over 48 kilo tonnes per annum.

sections.label: hydrogen commercial viability around 2040
sections.summary: In reply to Mr Liang Eng Hwa, the current assessment is that hydrogen will only be commercially viable around 2040.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: In reply to Mr Liang Eng Hwa, our current assessment is that hydrogen will only be commercially viable around 2040.

sections.label: Infrastructure costs of generation
sections.summary: Lower generation cost may be offset by added costs from landing sites, subsea interconnections, back-up and grid enhancements.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: While the cost of generation may be lower, infrastructure enhancements in the form of additional landing sites, subsea interconnections, back-up and grid enhancements will add to overall costs.

sections.label: Singapore maximum solar potential study
sections.summary: The Minister cited a study finding Singapore can reach a maximum solar potential of eight gigawatts peak by 2050, contributing only 10% of energy demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
sentences.text: The Minister cited a study that found that Singapore can only reach a maximum solar potential of eight gigawatts peak by 2050 and this will contribute to only 10% of energy demand.

sections.label: SERIS study and renewable energy proportion
sections.summary: The SERIS study factored in technology improvements and new deployment ways, and the allocated renewable energy proportion can flex upwards as solar and renewable developments improve.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: The study by SERIS has taken in improvements in technology and it has also factored in new ways of deployment.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: However, as what the hon Member has also alluded to, technology keeps improving all the time.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: So, we have allocated a certain proportion of our energy mix – because it is one of our four switches – for renewable energy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
sentences.text: And as long as the developments in solar power, in renewable energy continue to improve, that proportion can also continue to flex upwards.
